Le projet vise à installer des systèmes d’énergie solaire dans des zones non couvertes par la Compagnie Ivoirienne d'Électricité (CIE) pour améliorer l'accès aux soins, en particulier dans les régions éloignées. Rôle de l’UCP Santé Nutrition Banque mondiale : L’UCP Santé Nutrition, appuyée par la Banque mondiale, joue un rôle central en tant que coordinateur local du projet. L’UCP est impliquée dans la sélection des sites des centres de santé, dans la planification logistique et dans le suivi des activités menées par UNOPS et les prestataires, afin de garantir la qualité et la pertinence des installations solaires en fonction des besoins locaux. Role Purpose Sous la supervision directe de l’Ingénieure Civile et sous la direction du Chef de Projet, les Ingénieur.e.s Civil.e.s seront responsables de la bonne exécution des travaux de construction et réhabilitation, de la gestion des bureaux de supervision et contrôle et sous-traitants pour garantir des ouvrages conformes aux normes de l’UNOPS et aux exigences de la Banque mondiale. Dans l'exercice de leurs fonctions, les Ingénieur.e.s Civil.e.s travaillent avec un minimum de supervision et assurent la liaison avec les responsables de soutien au programme de l'UNOPS, les conseillers techniques en chef, les gestionnaires de portefeuille et les assistants de portefeuille afin d'assurer le meilleur soutien. Functions / Key Results Expected Assurance Qualité des Travaux Surveillance des Travaux sur le Terrain : Effectuer des visites régulières sur les sites de construction pour évaluer la qualité des travaux réalisés par les sous-traitants. Assurer le respect des spécifications techniques et de la qualité des matériaux utilisés. Contrôle de Conformité des Matériaux : Inspecter et valider les matériaux et équipements utilisés pour s’assurer de leur conformité aux spécifications techniques approuvées. Gestion des Non-Conformités : Identifier et documenter les déviations par rapport aux standards de qualité ou aux spécifications. Proposer des mesures correctives et assurer le suivi de leur mise en œuvre jusqu’à résolution complète. Supervision de la Sécurité : S’assurer que les protocoles de sécurité sont strictement respectés par toutes les parties impliquées dans le projet, en accord avec les règles de santé et sécurité d'UNOPS et de la Banque mondiale. Gestion des Risques Techniques et Résolution des Problèmes Identification des Risques : Évaluer les risques techniques, financiers, et de calendrier liés à chaque étape des travaux. Établir des plans d’atténuation et proposer des mesures correctives en cas de déviations. Résolution des Problèmes : Collaborer avec les sous-traitants et les équipes de projet pour résoudre les défis techniques rencontrés sur les sites. S’assurer que les problèmes sont abordés de manière proactive pour minimiser les retards et les coûts supplémentaires. Rapports de Risques : Préparer des rapports réguliers sur les risques techniques et les mesures prises pour les atténuer. Soumettre ces rapports au Chef de Projet et proposer des solutions pour les risques persistants. Contrôle et Suivi de l'Avancement des Travaux Établissement d’un Système de Suivi : Contribuer à la mise en place un système de suivi rigoureux pour chaque phase du projet, en validant l’état d’avancement des travaux et les activités clés présentés par les bureaux d’études. Assurer la rédaction des comptes rendus de réunions de chantier. Suivi des Échéances et des Budgets : Veiller à ce que chaque étape soit réalisée dans les délais et les budgets convenus. En cas de déviation, proposer des ajustements pour respecter les engagements. Réunions de Coordination : Organiser des réunions de suivi avec les sous-traitants, les bureaux d’études, et les partenaires pour s’assurer que tous les acteurs sont alignés sur les objectifs et les exigences du projet. Inspection Finale : Effectuer les inspections finales des travaux pour valider la conformité des installations avec les spécifications techniques et rédiger les documents de réception finale. Contribution au Partage des Connaissances et au Renforcement des Capacités Formation des Partenaires Locaux : Assister le personnel local et les sous-traitants dans l’acquisition de compétences techniques sur les standards de qualité et de sécurité. Organiser des sessions de formation pour garantir une compréhension uniforme des exigences du projet. Documentation des Leçons Apprises : Identifier et documenter les leçons apprises et les meilleures pratiques en matière de gestion de la qualité pour les projets d’infrastructure. Partager ces informations avec l’équipe de projet pour les appliquer dans des projets futurs. Participation aux Réseaux de Connaissance : Contribuer aux communautés de pratique de l’UNOPS, en partageant des études de cas, des rapports techniques, et des retours d’expérience sur le terrain pour renforcer l’efficacité des projets similaires. Souhaitée Une certification professionnelle en gestion de la qualité, en assurance qualité ou dans un domaine technique connexe est un atout (par exemple, ISO, Lean Six Sigma). Requirements Experience Requirements Requis Minimum de 2 ans d’expérience en ingénierie civile, incluant le contrôle de la qualité et la supervision de travaux d’infrastructure. Un diplôme de Master peut remplacer les deux (2) ans d'expérience significative requises Souhaitée Expérience préalable de travail en Afrique de l’Ouest ou dans un environnement similaire, avec des compétences démontrées en gestion de projets d’infrastructure.

review_candidates.title: VP, Strategic Finance
review_candidates.description: Team: Finance (G&A) Reports to: Chief Financial Officer Location: London, Amsterdam or Stockholm. Remote-first, with travel as and when needed About Nivoda Nivoda is the B2B marketplace rebuilding how the jewellery industry works. We connect independent jewellery retailers with a global network of diamond and gemstone suppliers, so a jeweller in Denver or Devon can source from anywhere in the world without the cost, risk, and hassle of doing it the old way. We handle the logistics, the payments, and the quality checks, the messy middle that used to put global sourcing out of reach for small businesses. Today we process over $300M in transactions a year in a $350B industry that still runs largely on personal relationships and paperwork. We are growing quickly, we are backed by leading investors, and we are only getting started. We built Nivoda so every jeweller, whatever their size and wherever they are, has access to the same global supply, pricing and tools as the biggest players. Why this role & why now You will sit on the Extended Leadership Team, report to the CFO, and own how Nivoda plans, reports and is funded. You will present to the board, investors and our receivables lender yourself, work directly with the CFO on equity and debt financing, and build a finance function that runs on routine rather than heroics. This is for someone who wants to lead a team and shape the company’s financial story, not only model it. What you will own Planning and forecasting. You own the annual budget, quarterly reforecast and long-range plan, plus scenario and funding cases for the C-suite and board. You are accountable for forecast accuracy against agreed tolerances, and for an honest post-mortem whether we miss or overachieve. Board, investor and lender reporting. You own the monthly board pack and the numbers behind it, plus materials for existing and prospective investors and our receivables lender, including covenant reporting and onsite diligence. You present to these audiences yourself and you are their first call for analytical questions. The aim is that they trust the numbers without the CFO needing to vouch for them. Corporate finance. You build the models and documentation for equity and debt financing, analyse term sheets, work with the People team on cap table and option pool, and support the CFO on transactions. Commercial and unit economics. You own cohort economics, customer lifetime value, geographic and segment profitability, and the return on marketing and sales spend. With the CRO’s organisation, you build quota and commission models so targets, incentives and the forecast point at the same numbers. Business partnering. You partner with Product and Engineering, Fulfilment, Fintech and the commercial teams on build versus buy, hiring cases, pricing and fee experiments, and capital allocation. The function says yes, no or not yet, with a model behind it. Leading the function. You lead the team: hiring, onboarding, objectives, development and performance, including written objectives and regular structured feedback for each person. You set the review standard and deliverables calendar, agree data contracts with the Data team, and own the tooling (Snowflake, NetSuite, ThoughtSpot, Claude and the modelling stack). We measure the function on on-time delivery, errors caught internally rather than by the audience, forecast accuracy, and how many people can produce each recurring deliverable. What good looks like First 90 days. You have taken over the monthly pack and the reforecast without the investors noticing a handover. You have met your leadership-team peers and told the CFO what you would change and in what order. 90 to 180 days. The monthly pack, FP&A-approved numbers and lender reporting land on the agreed date, each with a named owner and a written process. No board, lender or investor number has needed restating. The first version of the business line P&Ls is delivered at day 180. Twelve months. The function delivers month-end and board commitments without you or the CFO stepping in, including when you are away. A team member has delivered a new analytical capability end to end. FP&A and the Data team work from one set of metric definitions. Board members, lenders and the leadership team rely on the numbers without asking the CFO to vouch for them. The standard A finance team has no quota. The thing it sells is trust, and trust is earned with accuracy a bar above the rest of the company and delivery on the date promised. Three things must not fail in this role. Timeliness: deadlines are commitments, not targets. Quality: every external-facing number reconciles to a primary source and has been reviewed by someone other than its author before it leaves the team. Capacity: within reason, not a constraint. The function absorbs the demands of a 450-person company by organising, prioritising and delegating. If capacity is a hard limit, you make the case for a hire or an automation with numbers, rather than letting the work slip. That is a high bar, and it is fair because the role comes with the means to meet it: people to delegate to, authority over how the team's week is spent, a budget line, and the standing to say no to the business with the CFO's backing. What You Bring A background in investment banking, FP&A or venture capital, building models that senior stakeholders made decisions on. You have led a team, directly or through managers, and you want the management part of this role. You have presented to boards, investors or lenders as the person answering the question, not the person who built the slide. A working understanding of marketplace dynamics: two-sided liquidity, take rates, usage-based revenue without a contract, and what FX does to all of it. Complex cohort modelling is native to you. You are comfortable in Snowflake and a modern BI tool, you treat AI tooling as part of the stack, and you would rather fix the pipeline than reformat the output every month. You are calm under pressure, low on ego and allergic to spin. You tell people the uncomfortable thing early. Useful but not required: receivables financing or lender reporting, a multi-jurisdiction group, NetSuite, or a business that trades physical goods across borders. What this role is not It is not a bigger version of a senior analyst role, and it is not where every difficult model gets built personally. If you are at your best as the smartest modeler in the room and would rather stay that way, this will frustrate you. It is also not a quiet seat. Month-end, board and lender deadlines are fixed, a 450-person company makes a lot of demands on finance, and you will regularly be the one saying no, with the CFO’s backing. If you want a purely advisory or slower-paced role, this isn’t it. What we offer Nivoda is a place where smart, driven people do the best work of their careers. We move fast, give ownership early, and don’t have layers of bureaucracy slowing things down. If you see a problem, you can fix it. Our current benefits include: Flexible working hours and a vibrant, remote-first company culture Unlimited holiday allowance Participation in our equity programme Genuine opportunities for growth: we promote from within and invest in your development The chance to join during an expansion phase and shape how Nivoda operates at scale Interview Process Screening conversation with Talent Acquisition Structured career-history interview with Hiring Manager Focus interview: you present a case study to a panel from Finance and the leadership team Final conversation with the C-suite Equal opportunity Nivoda is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. If you meet most of this description and not all of it, apply anyway and tell us where the gaps are. Please submit your CV in English. Not the right role? Join our Talent Pool If this isn’t quite the right fit but you’re excited about what Nivoda is building, we’d still love to hear from you. Join our Talent Pool and we’ll reach out when the right opportunity comes along. nivoda.com/careers

review_candidates.description: Job Description Summary The position of General Manager, International Imaging Guided Systems (IGS), is responsible for developing and executing marketing strategies focused on increasing performance for the IGS business in the International Region. The International Region is comprised of the following geographies: Europe, Middle East, Africa, Russia, LatAm, Japan, AKA, India and South Asia. Key responsibilities for the role include a focus on offering development, channel strategy, strategic pricing and commercial execution, coordinating across product lines, services and solutions. This role is responsible within the International Region for selling product(s), services, parts, solutions, or projects and for driving growth by working across P&L and regional marketing & sales teams. The General Manager will gather voice of the customer and provide customer input on product and solutions definitions and requirements. In addition, he/she will collaborate with relevant commercial and product marketing teams, Global Strategic Marketing, and Marketing Communications to develop innovative strategies for the modality. As part of the International Imaging leadership team and directly reporting to the global general manager IGS, the Modality General Manager defines the proper channels (Direct, Indirect, Digital, etc.), the “go to market” strategy for the region and the commercial intensity programs on which to focus. The segment manager is responsible for the quarterly and yearly Orders/Sales forecast for the region, the yearly region’s target setting and the achievements versus targets. La région International comprend l’Europe, le Moyen-Orient, l'Afrique, la Russie, l'Amérique latine, le Japon, AKA, l'Inde et South Asia. Les responsabilités clés de ce rôle incluent le développement de l'offre, la stratégie des canaux de distribution, la tarification stratégique, l’exécution commerciale et la coordination à travers les lignes de produits, les services et les solutions.
